text:
elyse: FYI pushed `deferred-kv` prototype. streams safetensors shards and hydrates layer KVs in background; serves while hydrate in-flight. need a contract so callers know layer readiness. objections?

devin: eviction thrash concern if hydrator populates and evictor reclaims. we should expose a short pin window (configurable).

raj_k: encrypted-header path can stall streamer. suggest manifest flags: `decrypt_priority` and `hydratable=false` for shards that must block-load.

maria: propose two minimal surfaces: 1) loader events on runtime bus (hydration_started/done/failed) and 2) a tiny HTTP query API: `GET /v1/weights/:model/hydration_state?layer=...` returning small envelope. define `ready` semantics.

elyse: prototype emits events but no query API yet. semantics question: does `ready` mean mapped, pinned, or just loaded?

devin: prefer conservative: `ready` = mapped in-process and pinned for `pin_ms` so callers get low-latency access. pin time pluggable.

raj_k: also add `warmup_hints` to manifests to prioritize layers (example: layers ["attn.kv","ff.0"], priority: "background", pin_ms:2000). loader must ignore unknown fields.

maria: telemetry: per-layer time_to_ready, hydration_cpu_ms, bytes_transferred, failure_code. surface alerts in Console (e.g., attn.kv > 300ms).

loader-bot: CI: deferred-kv tests passed 12/14; flaky in encrypted-header path.

elyse: fallback now retries decrypt then blocks; flaky. alternate: mark non-hydratable shards in manifest to trigger blocking hotload by default.

devin: push events vs polling? push nice but infra cost.

raj_k: support both. minimal event envelope: {model, shard_id, layer, state, ts, progress, failure_code?}. keep small.

maria: will mock dashboard panels and alerts.

elyse: action items: (1) i'll open RFC for hydration_state query + event envelope; (2) raj will draft manifest schema; (3) devin will draft eviction/pin semantics; (4) maria will list telemetry and alert rules. target: 2 weeks. note: hydration_state is per-instance only, not global model readiness.
